methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective observational study of 564 patients with appropriate training/validation split (7:3), multivariate logistic regression, and internal validation using bootstrap resampling (1000 repetitions). Double-blind ultrasound review by multiple radiologists with arbitration mechanism for disagreement. Limitations: retrospective design with inherent selection bias; relatively small EC cohort (n=89) compared to control (n=475) affecting power; no external validation reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Case-control retrospective study (LoE 4) demonstrating diagnostic and prognostic utility of transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) heterogeneous endometrial echogenicity combined with clinical risk factors for endometrial cancer screening. High clinical relevance for non-invasive EC risk stratification; validated nomogram provides quantitative individualized risk assessment. Addresses gap in early EC diagnosis tool development.

reporting_quality.justification: Retrospective diagnostic/prognostic study following REMARK reporting standards with clear diagnostic criteria, patient selection, imaging standardization (IETA terminology), and pathological reference standards. Comprehensive reporting of sensitivity/specificity, ROC analysis, and calibration metrics. However, no explicit statement regarding data availability, code sharing, or repository deposition. Limited information on reproducibility of nomogram outside institutional setting.

novelty_literature.justification: Meaningful incremental contribution integrating TVS heterogeneous echogenicity (known imaging feature) with multiple clinical risk factors (BMI, hypertension, diabetes, age at menopause) into a single nomogram prediction model. SHAP interpretability analysis adds modern methodological rigor. However, component risk factors (obesity, diabetes, hypertension, menopause age) and TVS features individually established; primary novelty is in multivariate integration and nomogram construction rather than discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear clinical motivation, detailed methods describing ultrasound technique using standardized IETA terminology, comprehensive results with appropriate statistical tables and figures, thorough discussion of pathophysiologic mechanisms linking risk factors to EC. Clinical case demonstrations enhance interpretability. Figure quality and table organization support manuscript clarity effectively.

key_strengths: Development of interpretable nomogram using SHAP analysis demonstrating that heterogeneous endometrial echogenicity and age at menopause are most influential predictors, enhancing clinical utility
Internal validation with excellent discrimination (AUC 0.958) and stable calibration in separate validation set; decision curve analysis confirms clinical net benefit across threshold range
Comprehensive ultrasound standardization using IETA consensus terminology with double-blind independent review by multiple radiologists and arbitration mechanism for diagnostic accuracy
Excellent agreement between nomogram predictions and actual outcomes: 93 predicted EC cases (16.49%) vs 89 actual cases (15.78%, P>0.05)
Thorough discussion linking EC risk factors to pathophysiologic mechanisms (estrogen-progesterone imbalance, insulin resistance, oxidative stress) grounding clinical findings in biology
key_concerns: Severe class imbalance in cohort: EC cases n=89 (15.8%) versus control n=475 (84.2%) may inflate discriminatory performance estimates and risk of overfitting; authors acknowledge high AUC 0.958 partly attributable to low event rate

Retrospective design with selection bias from symptomatic population (patients with abnormal vaginal bleeding, postmenopausal bleeding); findings may not generalize to asymptomatic screening populations
Single-center institution study (Ninth Medical Center, PLA General Hospital); external validation in independent cohorts essential before clinical implementation

No external validation reported; internal validation adequate but does not address generalizability across healthcare systems, equipment types (different ultrasound systems), or operator expertise variation
No data availability statement; unclear whether nomogram/code available for external use or validation in other centers
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent retrospective diagnostic study with novel integration of imaging and clinical factors into interpretable prediction tool. Excellent internal performance but class imbalance, single-center design, and lack of external validation limit tier placement to 3 (4-9.9 JIF). Minor revisions should address overfitting concerns and plan external validation.
